resources.string: Simulation — not investment advice. All prices and funds are virtual.
Tap or long-press chart to inspect OHLC · Pinch to zoom
The gap between the highest Bid (sell) price and lowest Ask (buy) price at a given tick. Entering via Market Order crosses the spread immediately.
Practice tip: Liquid assets like BPAT or XVMG have tight spreads, while low-liquidity tokens like KPSW have wider spreads.
The extra price movement between your expected execution price and actual fill price when a large Market or Stop order absorbs available tick liquidity.
Practice tip: Split oversized orders or use Limit orders on thinner assets to keep slippage low.
A pre-planned exit trigger that automatically closes your position if price moves against you, capping worst-case loss before emotions take over.
Practice tip: Place your Stop-Loss at a logical chart invalidation level, not randomly after already losing.
One-Cancels-the-Other pairs a Take-Profit limit order and a Stop-Loss order on the same position. When one fills, the other cancels automatically.
Practice tip: Attaching OCO when opening a trade enforces your Risk/Reward plan from the very first tick.
A multiplier (e.g., 3x or 5x) allowing larger exposure with smaller locked margin. Both gains AND losses are multiplied equally, plus per-tick borrow fees.
Practice tip: High leverage amplifies minor noise into forced liquidation. Master 1x spot sizing first.
Margin Level = Equity / Leveraged Margin. At 110% or below you enter Margin Call; at 100% or below, losing leveraged positions are force-closed to protect solvency.
Practice tip: Always pair leveraged or short trades with a Stop-Loss well above the liquidation price.
The largest percentage drop from your portfolio\'s historical peak equity to a subsequent trough before recovering to a new peak.
Practice tip: A 50% drawdown requires a +100% gain just to break even. Keeping max drawdown under 10–15% is crucial.
Compares average profit on winning trades against average loss on losing trades. A 2.0 ratio means winners earn 2x what losers lose.
Practice tip: With a 1.5+ Risk/Reward ratio, you can stay profitable even with a 45% win rate.
Each bar summarizes Open, High, Low, and Close within a timeframe. Long wicks show price rejection, while full bodies show strong directional control.
Practice tip: Always read candles alongside the current Market Regime rather than trading a single bar blindly.
Never risk more than 1–2% of total account equity on a single trade\'s Stop-Loss distance: Units = (Equity × Risk%) / |Entry − StopLoss|.
Practice tip: Even 10 consecutive Stop-Loss hits at 1% risk still leave ~90% of your capital intact.
